evidence: Cic. Off. 1.53: ejusdem gentis, nātiōnis, linguae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly a Roman clan; in a wider sense a race or people, beside nātiō and populus. “Racial” is the genitive: gentis, generis (“of race”).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.286: malō genere nātus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Birth and descent, the stock a person comes from; also “kind, sort” in general. genus hūmānum is the human race (see human).

evidence: M-O s.v. race (classification of humans; Egger)
terms.comment: Literally the stock of a plant, then a family line. Morgan–Owens gives it, after Egger, for race as a classification of people.
aliēnigena is classical (Cic., Liv.), one born abroad; Morgan–Owens offers this, or invidia in aliēnigenās, for racial prejudice.

phrases.latin: propior est ejusdem gentis, nātiōnis, linguae, quā maximē hominēs conjunguntur
phrases.english: closer is the bond of the same race, nation and language, by which people are most closely joined
